title: Large-area Scanning Probe Nanolithography Facilitated by Automated Alignment and Its Application to Substrate Fabrication for Cell Culture Studies
protocol: Add 10 µL of platinum(0)-1,3-divinyl-1,1,3,3-tetramethyldisiloxane complex solution to 250 g of (7-8 % w/w vinylmethylsiloxane)-dimethylsiloxane co-polymer.
Add 172 µL of 1,3,5,7-tetramethyl-1,3,5,7-tetravinylcyclotetrasiloxane to the mixture.
Mix these components thoroughly on a rotary mixer for 7 days.
Add 0.5 g of (25-35 % w/w methylhydrosiloxane)-dimethylsiloxane co-polymer to a 1.7 g portion of the previously mixed solution in a weighing boat.
Mix thoroughly with a spatula.
Degas this mixture by transferring it to a vacuum desiccator and exposing it to low pressure (200 mTorr, 0.3 mBar) for 20 min until all gas bubbles have dissipated.
Place a 13 x 13 mm glass slide in a plastic screw-topped vial filled with 20 mL of 2-propanol.
Place the vial in an ultrasonic bath for 10 min to remove large debris.
Wash the slides by submerging them in fresh 2-propanol (100 mL).
Dry the slides under a stream of nitrogen gas.
Place a silicon master into a 4 cm diameter petri dish.
Add sufficient degassed PDMS prepolymer mixture until fully covering the master.
Degas the polymer in a vacuum desiccator for 5 minutes.
Treat glass squares with O2 plasma at 600 mTorr and maximum RF power for 1 minute.
Place the O2 plasma-treated slide over the prepolymer on the silicon master, plasma-cleaned side down.
Gently press down the glass slide to remove trapped air.
Place the sandwiched PDMS array in a petri dish with the silicon master at the bottom.
Cure the PDMS in an oven at 70−80 °C for 24−48 hours.
Remove the cured array from the oven and allow to cool for 15 min.
Carefully remove any excess PDMS from the back and sides of the glass slide with a razor blade.
Use a stream of dry nitrogen to blow away any loose PDMS debris.
Wedge a razor blade into the corner of the array at a depth of 1 mm and carefully pry the array apart from the master in one continuous lifting action.
Carefully cut and scrape away 0.5 mm of the PDMS at the edges of the array with a razor blade.
Use a stream of dry nitrogen to blow away any loose PDMS debris.
Place the PPL pen array in a petri dish into plasma chamber.
Apply vacuum to 600 mTorr.
Switch on the plasma generator (maximum setting) for 30 s.
Release the vacuum and remove the array from the treatment apparatus.
Check the hydrophilicity of the array by dropping 20 µL of deionized water on its surface.
If the water does not spread evenly, subject the array to a second round of plasma treatment.
Dry the treated array thoroughly with a stream of dry nitrogen gas.
Attach the array onto the middle of the probe holder using double-sided carbon tape.
Mount the probe holder onto the AFM kinematic holder.
Prepare 1 mM 16-mercaptohexadecanoic acid (MHA) solution by dissolving 8.6 mg in 30 mL ethanol and placing it in an ultrasonic bath for 10 minutes.
Deposit 20 µL of MHA solution on the array using a micropipette, avoiding contact with the pipette tips.
Allow the MHA solution to spread across the array surface.
Let the ethanol evaporate under ambient conditions until dry.
Mount the probe holder with the PPL array onto the AFM.
Place the gold substrate in the middle of the AFM sample stage and secure it with adhesive tape around the borders of the substrate.
Adjust the stage height using the z-axis controller according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Open and run the stage controller setup program (SetupNSF.exe) on the computer to reset all axes and angles to a pre-calibrated zero point.
Switch the stage release lever to release the sample stage.
Activate the triad of force sensors as indicated by the AFM manufacturer's instructions.
Allow the force sensors to equilibrate for at least 15 min.
Increase the z-axis height to bring the array into close proximity with the substrate by visually observing the probe array and surface.
Open/run the Automatic Alignment program (Auto Alignment v16.exe).
Enter relevant alignment parameters into the program.
Enter the desired 'Angle Step' parameter value, typically 0.15°.
Set the 'Coarse Step' parameter value, typically 0.6 µm.
Configure the 'Excel file path' and attach an unmodified copy of the provided spreadsheet template file by using the 'folder' icon, navigating to the file location, and pressing 'OK'.
Open/run the AFM control software.
Navigate to the spectroscopy component of this program by clicking the 'spectroscopy' button.
Set the AFM scan head z-axis to oscillate by 10 µm over 100 ms, with a pause time of 250 ms.
Retract the AFM scan head 10 µm over 100 ms with a pause time of 250 ms.
Click the 'start' button of the alignment software to begin the automated alignment process.
Do not use the stage controller consoles during the alignment process.
Inspect the graphs in the spreadsheet template file for correlation between recorded data points and the line fit generated by the software.
Replace the probe array with a newly prepared array if alignment is unsuccessful.
Move the stage upwards in the z-axis using 500 nm increments until contact can be observed.
Click the 'stop' button on the AFM control software to stop the spectroscopy program from step 4.5.
Retract the array by 10 μm.
Check the image from the top view camera of the AFM to ensure that the probes are not in contact with the substrate.
Navigate to the lithography component of the control software by clicking the 'lithography' button on control software.
Choose the z-modulation operating mode.
Import a raster (bitmap) or vector image for the lithography pattern.
Use a bitmap consisting 20 x 20 black pixels, corresponding to a grid of 20 x 20 dots per probe on the PPL array.
Enter the lithography parameters into the 'Pixel Graphic Import' window of the AFM controller software.
Configure the 'Size' of the pattern to be generated, e.g., 40 µm in length and width.
Set the origin of the pattern at 25 µm on both x and y axes.
Select 'Modulation Abs Z Pos' from the drop-down menu.
Simplify to two layers.
Set the values in the 'Black (0)' field to 5 µm.
Set the values in the 'White (1)' field to -5 µm.
Click the 'OK' button to implement these settings and close the window.
Enter the 'pause time' in the lithography window of the AFM control software, typically 1 s.
Prepare the atmospheric control enclosure.
Lower the atmospheric isolation chamber onto the AFM.
Open and run the manufacturer-supplied atmospheric control software (MHG_control.exe).
Set the relative humidity to 45% in the atmospheric control software.
Set the temperature to 25 °C in the atmospheric control software.
Set the atmosphere exchange flow rate to 500 mL in the atmospheric control software.
Click 'Use' to implement the settings.
Start the lithographic sequence by pressing the 'start' button on the software interface.
Once lithography is complete, use the z-axis stage controller console to move the substrate away from the array by retracting the stage by 500 µm.
Remove the atmospheric isolation chamber from its mount.
Switch the stage release lever to lock the sample stage.
Deactivate the force sensors as indicated by the AFM manufacturer's instructions.
Remove the substrate from the stage.
Scan the patterned surface on AFM with lateral force mode using a contact mode cantilever.
Prepare aqueous solutions of 40 mM thiourea, 27 mM iron(III) nitrate, and 100 mM hydrochloric acid.
Mix 5 mL of each solution to prepare the etchant.
Freshly mix the etchant prior to each use.
Transfer the patterned substrate into a petri dish.
Pipette sufficient etchant solution to cover the surface of the substrate (typically 10 mL).
Submerge the substrate for 4-5 min to etch 15 nm of gold.
Remove the substrate and thoroughly rinse with water.
Dry the substrate with a stream of nitrogen.
Inspect the etched gold features under bright field optical microscopy.
If the entire surface appears homogeneous, repeat the etching step for 1-2 min.
Immerse the patterned substrates into a solution of 1 mM (11-mercaptoundecyl)hexa(ethylene glycol) in ethanol for 1 h.
Wash the substrate three times with ethanol.
Dry the substrate thoroughly under a stream of nitrogen.
Submerge the substrates in a 10 mM Co(NO3)2 aqueous solution for 5 min.
Remove the substrates from the Co(NO3)2 solution.
Wash the substrates three times with ultrapure water.
Dry the substrates under a stream of dry nitrogen.
Immerse the substrate in a 50 µg/mL fibronectin solution in phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Incubate the substrate at 4 °C for 16 h.
Wash the substrate three times with PBS.
Dry the substrate under a stream of dry nitrogen.
Apply a 2 mL solution of 1:100 unconjugated rabbit anti-fibronectin primary antibody in 5% (w/v) bovine serum albumin (BSA) in PBS to the surface.
Incubate at 4 °C for 16 h.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash the substrate three times with PBS.
Submerge the substrate in a 2 mL solution of fluorescently conjugated anti-rabbit secondary antibody (at the manufacturer's specified dilution, typically 2 drops/mL) in 5% (w/v) BSA in PBS.
Cover the substrate with tin foil.
Incubate at room temperature for 1 hour.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Wash three times with PBS.
Record epifluorescence microscopy images of the features using a fluorescence microscope according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Set the excitation filter to 594 nm.
Prepare a suspension of well-characterized hMSCs that are between the 4th and 6th passage.
Rinse once with 10 mL PBS.
Dissociate adhered cells by adding 5 mL of trypsin/EDTA into the T75 tissue culture flask.
Incubate in a humidified chamber at 37 °C supplemented with 5% CO2 for up to 5 min until 90% of cells are detached from surface.
Add 6 mL of fresh culture media containing 10% fetal calf serum (FCS) into the flask and briefly rinse the flask with the added media.
Transfer cell suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 400 g at 25 °C for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend cell pellet in 3 mL of fresh culture media.
Count the cell density using a hemocytometer.
Adjust the density of the cell suspension to 2 x 10^4 cells/mL by adding an appropriate volume of culture media.
Seed the cells onto substrates at a density of 10^4 cells/cm^2.
Cut the substrate into 1 x 1 cm² with a diamond scribe.
Place the substrate in a well of a 12-well tissue culture plate.
Pipette 2 mL of cell suspension in culture media into the well.
Incubate the well in a humidified chamber at 37 °C supplemented with 5% CO₂ for 24 h.
Remove the medium from the well.
Wash the substrates once with PBS.
Fix cells with 2 mL of a solution of 4% paraformaldehyde in PBS (pre-warmed to 37 °C) for 20 min in a fume hood.
Wash the substrate three times with PBS.
Permeabilize the cells with 2 mL of a solution of 0.5% detergent in PBS for 15 min.
Wash the substrate three times with PBS.
Submerge the substrate in 2 mL of a solution of unconjugated rabbit anti-fibronectin primary antibody at dilution of 1:100 with 5% (w/v) BSA in PBS and incubate at 4 °C for 16 h.
Wash the substrate three times with 0.1% (v/v) Tween 20 in PBS (PBST).
Submerge the substrate in 2 mL of a solution of fluorescently conjugated anti-rabbit secondary antibody diluted with 5% (w/v) BSA in PBS at the manufacturer's specified dilution.
Incubate the substrate covered in tin foil at room temperature for 1 h.
Wash the substrate three times with 0.1% PBST.
Mix 2 mL of fluorescently conjugated phalloidin at a dilution of 1:250 in PBS.
Cover the solution in tin foil.
Incubate at 4 °C for 30 min.
Wash three times with PBS.
Apply a drop of mounting medium containing DAPI to stain cell nuclei and mount the substrate.
Cover the sample with a coverslip.
Visualize cells using a fluorescence microscope according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Use an excitation filter of 365 nm for nuclei (DAPI).
Use an excitation filter of 488 nm for F-actin.
Use an excitation filter of 594 nm for fibronectin.
